title: What Goes Into Your Medical Discharge File Before Leaving Türkiye

metaDescription: Collect 8 mandatory English medical discharge documents before leaving Türkiye, from operative notes and implant cards to imaging and fit-to-fly.
quickAnswer: A complete medical discharge file turkey packet should be collected in English before you check out of your hotel. Ensure it holds eight essential items: your operative report, anesthesia summary, discharge epicrisis, implant or device serial cards, pre- and post-op imaging, medication prescriptions, itemized official invoice, and signed Fit-to-Fly clearance.

body.text: Once your plane leaves Istanbul, chasing missing hospital records across time zones becomes slow and stressful. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), we are an independent, client-paid, flat-fee travel, business, and medical travel advisory run by our two founders in Türkiye—paid by our clients and independent of provider commissions. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions. Itinerary of Türkiye does not provide clinical advice or emergency medical care, and we help you build practical document-collection checkpoints into your itinerary before departure.
What 8 mandatory documents (operative report, implant serial cards, CBCT/imaging, prescriptions, itemized invoice, fit-to-fly) must you collect?

Before leaving Türkiye, collect eight core documents in English from your hospital or clinic: the signed operative report, anesthesia record, hospital discharge summary (epicrisis), manufacturer implant serial cards, all diagnostic imaging (CBCT, X-rays, ultrasound, or lab panels), generic medication prescriptions, an itemized official invoice, and your dated Fit-to-Fly certificate.

Under [European Commission MDCG 2019-8 Implant Card Guidance (EU MDR 2017/745)](https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2020-09/md_mdcg_2019_8_implant_guidance_card_en_0.pdf), implantable device cards must specify the device name, manufacturer, serial or lot number, Unique Device Identifier (UDI), and implanting institution—details that matter for dental implants, breast implants, orthopedic hardware, and bariatric bands alike.

body.text: Why do home-country doctors need English surgical notes?

Home-country physicians, dentists, and emergency room teams cannot safely diagnose swelling, infection, or hardware issues without knowing exactly what was performed inside the operating room. Complete English surgical notes eliminate guesswork around surgical anatomy, implanted materials, antibiotic resistance, and which sutures or drains were placed.

Both [UK Travel Aware Surgery Abroad Guidance](https://travelaware.campaign.gov.uk/surgery-abroad-cut-out-the-risk/) and [NaTHNaC TravelHealthPro Medical Tourism Guidance](https://travelhealthpro.org.uk/factsheets/travelling-for-treatment-medical-tourism) emphasize bringing back full English medical reports, X-rays, and scans for your home clinician. Local Turkish medication brand names often differ from US, UK, or EU brands, so having the generic active ingredient (such as amoxicillin/clavulanate or enoxaparin) written clearly prevents dangerous dosing errors after you land.
How do you verify your discharge file is complete before hotel checkout?

Schedule a dedicated 20-minute document review at your final post-op clinic visit—at least 24 hours before your flight—so administrative staff can fix spelling errors, add missing physician stamps, or export digital DICOM files while you are still physically in Istanbul.
Never accept a promise that records "will be emailed next week" as your only copy. Run through this verification checklist before leaving the clinic:

items: Check Name & Passport Spelling: Confirm your legal name and date of birth match your passport across every page.
Verify Official Stamps & Signatures: Ensure the operative report, prescriptions, and Fit-to-Fly letter carry the doctor's signature and hospital stamp.
Open Digital Scans on the Spot: If CBCT or X-ray files are provided on a USB drive or download link, open them before leaving to confirm they are not corrupt or password-locked.
Match Implant Stickers to Physical Cards: Check that dental or surgical implant batch stickers match the exact number of implants placed.
Keep Originals in Carry-On: Place the physical folder in your cabin bag alongside your medications—never inside checked luggage.

body.text: How should you back up digital copies?

Create two independent digital backups before boarding: scan every paper page into a single clear PDF saved offline on your phone, and upload an encrypted copy (along with DICOM imaging files) to a password-protected cloud drive shared with one trusted family member or travel companion.

Using clear filenames—such as 2026-Operative-Report-Istanbul.pdf and 2026-Implant-Serial-Cards.pdf—makes retrieval fast in a stressful ER waiting room. Keep offline copies accessible even without mobile data during your flight. faq.q: Can a Turkish clinic refuse to give me my operative report in English?
faq.a: Licensed international health tourism facilities in Türkiye are expected to provide clear medical documentation to foreign patients. Confirm in writing before booking that your full discharge packet will be issued in English prior to departure.

faq.q: Do I need DICOM files for dental CBCT scans, or is a printed picture enough?
faq.a: Request both a PDF summary and the raw DICOM files on a USB drive or secure download link. Home-country dentists and oral surgeons need DICOM data to view 3D bone and implant angles accurately.

faq.q: Why do airport customs officers care about my Turkish prescriptions?
faq.a: Carrying stamped English prescriptions listing generic drug names proves that antibiotics, painkillers, or injectable blood thinners in your carry-on bag were legally prescribed for your surgery.

faq.q: What if I received dental crowns instead of implants—do I still need material cards?
faq.a: Yes. Ask for the dental laboratory certificate listing the exact ceramic or zirconia brand, shade code, and cement type used, which helps your home dentist handle future repairs.

faq.q: Should I email my discharge file to Itinerary of Türkiye for safekeeping?
faq.a: No. You should keep your private medical records solely with yourself, your healthcare providers, and your trusted personal backup—Itinerary of Türkiye coordinates travel logistics and does not store clinical files.

faq.q: When should my Fit-to-Fly letter be dated?
faq.a: Your Fit-to-Fly certificate should be issued and dated after your final post-op physical examination, typically 24 to 48 hours before your scheduled departure from Türkiye.
